packet.headline_seed: Australia news live: arrival of H5N1 bird flu a ‘genuine wildlife emergency’, experts say; fuel excise rebate extended for extra month
packet.description_seed: Follow live updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast And welcome to another Sunday Guardian live blog. We’ll continue to bring you the latest news and reactions following confirmation of Australia’s first mainland case of deadly H5 bird flu , as well as the government’s extension to fuel excise cuts for a further month. A “swim out” event is planned for Sydney’s Coogee beach marking one week since a woman was bitten, suffering critical injuries. Continue reading...

clean_source_blocks.text: Follow live updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast And welcome to another Sunday Guardian live blog. We’ll continue to bring you the latest news and reactions following confirmation of Australia’s first mainland case of deadly H5 bird flu , as well as the government’s extension to fuel excise cuts for a further month. A “swim out” event is planned for Sydney’s Coogee beach marking one week since a woman was bitten, suffering critical injuries. Continue reading...

The federal government confirmed on Saturday that mainland Australia had its first case of the deadly H5N1 bird flu strain that has devastated wildlife populations globally. Australia had been the last continent free of the disease. If it becomes established in wild native bird populations it could have catastrophic effects. In case you missed this development, let’s recap the key details: The infected migratory seabird – a brown skua – was found on the coast at Cape Le Grand national park near Esperance in southern Western Australia last Sunday and has since died.

The bird, which was found unwell last Sunday, had died from H5N1, testing positive for the deadly flu, said Ms Collins. Another bird, a sick giant petrel, found in the same area is also found to be infected, tests taken in Western Australia suggested. Up until the authorities announced, Australia was the last remaining continent which had not reported the virulent strain of H5 bird flu. It was last confirmed on Heard Island, a sub-Antarctic Australian territory in late 2025. The bird flu has spread through wild bird and mammal populations since 2021, killing millions, infecting poultry and dairy farms and even some ​farmworkers. On Saturday, prime minister Albanese said the arrival of H5N1 bird flu was "concerning" and the government was taking steps to limit its spread and has already spent $113m in preparation.

The Invasive Species Council (ISC) and the Australian Marine Conservation Society (AMCS) have called for an extra $200m in funding over the next two years. AMCS campaigns director Alexia Wellbelove said H5 bird flu posed a real risk to the future of species such as the Australian sea lion, which was already endangered and existed nowhere else on earth. ISC chief executive Jack Gough said “whether this particular outbreak is contained or not, the threat is no longer theoretical”: This is a genuine wildlife emergency and it must be treated as such with emergency funding to increase efforts to protect wildlife populations. Agriculture minister says investigations under way into mainland spread of H5N1 bird flu

Kate Millar, chief executive of BirdLife Australia, said the significance for Australian wildlife of the arrival of H5N1 bird flu could not be overstated and it could be “the beginning of a long fight to protect birds and wildlife in Australia”:

The potential for this virus to kill wildlife in significant numbers means it could be particularly catastrophic for threatened species.

We are talking about possible extinctions, alongside severe impacts to common birds like our beloved pelicans and black swans.

Millar said she was concerned “many jurisdictions at the local level simply don’t yet have plans in place to respond to H5 bird flu” and called for a rapid increase in investment in conservation programs to ensure people could respond.

The Invasive Species Council (ISC) and the Australian Marine Conservation Society (AMCS) have called for an extra $200m in funding over the next two years.

AMCS campaigns director Alexia Wellbelove said H5 bird flu posed a real risk to the future of species such as the Australian sea lion, which was already endangered and existed nowhere else on earth.

ISC chief executive Jack Gough said “whether this particular outbreak is contained or not, the threat is no longer theoretical”:

This is a genuine wildlife emergency and it must be treated as such with emergency funding to increase efforts to protect wildlife populations.

Agriculture minister says investigations under way into mainland spread of H5N1 bird flu

"We, of course, always examine these issues carefully. We have prepared for it," the prime minister said.

payload.title: H5N1-lintuinfluenssa todettiin ensi kertaa Australian mantereella
payload.summary: Australian viranomaiset ovat vahvistaneet H5N1-lintuinfluenssan ensimmäisen mantereella todetun tapauksen. Luontojärjestöt varoittavat vakavasta uhasta luonnonvaraisille eläimille ja vaativat lisärahoitusta suojelutoimiin.
payload.content:
Australian liittovaltion hallitus on vahvistanut, että H5N1-lintuinfluenssa on todettu ensi kertaa maan mantereella. Tartunta löytyi muuttavalta merilinnulta Länsi-Australian etelärannikolla, ja luontojärjestöt varoittavat viruksen voivan aiheuttaa vakavia seurauksia, jos se vakiintuu luonnonvaraisiin lintukantoihin.

## Tartunta löytyi Länsi-Australian rannikolta

Tartunnan saanut lintu oli ruskea etelänkiisla, joka löydettiin huonokuntoisena Cape Le Grandin kansallispuiston rannikolta lähellä Esperancea Eteläisessä Länsi-Australiassa viime sunnuntaina. Lintu on sittemmin kuollut, ja testit vahvistivat sen sairastaneen H5N1-lintuinfluenssaa.

Samalta alueelta löydetyn sairastuneen jättiläismyrskylinnun testeissä on myös viitteitä tartunnasta. Viranomaiset selvittävät nyt, miten H5N1 on levinnyt Australian mantereelle. Ennen ilmoitusta Australiaa pidettiin viimeisenä maanosana, jossa tätä voimakkaasti leviävää H5-lintuinfluenssan kantaa ei ollut raportoitu mantereella.

Australian alueista tauti oli kuitenkin vahvistettu jo loppuvuonna 2025 Heardinsaarella, joka on subantarktinen Australian territorio. H5N1 on vuodesta 2021 lähtien levinnyt luonnonvaraisissa lintu- ja nisäkäspopulaatioissa eri puolilla maailmaa. Se on tappanut miljoonia eläimiä ja aiheuttanut tartuntoja myös siipikarjassa, maitotiloilla ja joissakin maataloustyöntekijöissä.

## Järjestöt vaativat lisärahoitusta

Pääministeri Anthony Albanese kuvasi H5N1:n saapumista huolestuttavaksi ja sanoi hallituksen ryhtyneen toimiin leviämisen rajoittamiseksi. Hänen mukaansa valmisteluihin on käytetty jo 113 miljoonaa dollaria.

Invasive Species Council ja Australian Marine Conservation Society vaativat lisäksi 200 miljoonan dollarin lisärahoitusta seuraavalle kahdelle vuodelle. AMCS:n kampanjajohtaja Alexia Wellbelove varoitti, että H5-lintuinfluenssa voi uhata esimerkiksi australianmerileijonan tulevaisuutta. Laji on jo valmiiksi uhanalainen ja elää vain Australiassa.

ISC:n johtaja Jack Goughin mukaan uhka ei ole enää teoreettinen riippumatta siitä, saadaanko tämä yksittäinen tartuntarypäs hallintaan. Hänen mukaansa kyse on todellisesta luonnonvaraisten eläinten hätätilanteesta, joka vaatii kiireellistä rahoitusta suojelutoimien vahvistamiseen.
